points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 德沃夏克出生于内拉霍齐采的一个小村庄，父亲是屠夫兼旅店老板。尽管家境贫寒，但父亲支持他的音乐天赋。他从小就展现出对音乐的浓厚兴趣，在村里的教堂学习小提琴和管风琴。这段乡村生活为他后来的创作注入了丰富的民间音乐元素，尤其是波西米亚和斯拉夫民族的音乐特色，成为他日后作品的重要源泉。
points.descriptionEn: Dvořák was born in the small village of Nelahozeves to a butcher and innkeeper father. Despite the family's modest circumstances, his father supported his musical talent. He showed early interest in music, learning violin and organ at the village church. This rural life infused his later compositions with rich folk music elements, particularly Bohemian and Slavic characteristics, which became a significant source for his future works.

points.title: 音乐求学
points.description: 德沃夏克前往布拉格，在布拉格管风琴学校学习。在这里，他接受了系统的音乐教育，学习了作曲理论和管风琴演奏。尽管经济困难，他靠演奏各种乐器维生，包括中提琴。这段时期，他接触到了莫扎特、贝多芬和瓦格纳等大师的作品，深受影响。1860年，他成为布拉格临时剧院的中提琴手，开始了他的职业音乐生涯。
points.descriptionEn: Dvořák moved to Prague to study at the Prague Organ School. Here he received systematic musical education, learning composition theory and organ playing. Despite financial difficulties, he made a living by playing various instruments, including the viola. During this period, he was deeply influenced by the works of masters like Mozart, Beethoven, and Wagner. In 1860, he became a violist at the Provisional Theatre in Prague, beginning his professional music career.

points.title: 创作成熟期
points.description: 1873年，德沃夏克辞去了剧院职务，专注于作曲。这一时期是他创作的黄金时代，创作了包括《斯拉夫舞曲》、《斯拉夫狂想曲》等民族风格鲜明的作品。1884年，他首次访问英国，受到热烈欢迎，并多次前往英国指挥自己的作品。1888年，他与勃拉姆斯建立了深厚的友谊，勃拉姆斯对他的创作给予了高度评价。1890年，他被任命为布拉格音乐学院教授，开始培养新一代音乐人才。
points.descriptionEn: In 1873, Dvořák resigned from his theatre position to focus on composition. This period marked his golden age of creativity, producing works with strong national character like the 'Slavonic Dances' and 'Slavonic Rhapsodies'. In 1884, he made his first visit to England, where he was warmly welcomed and frequently returned to conduct his own works. In 1888, he developed a deep friendship with Brahms, who highly praised his compositions. In 1890, he was appointed professor at the Prague Conservatory, beginning to nurture the next generation of musical talent.

points.title: 美国岁月
points.description: 德沃夏克受邀担任纽约国家音乐学院院长，在美国度过了三年。这段时期，他创作了著名的《新世界交响曲》，融合了美国黑人灵歌和印第安音乐元素。他还创作了《美国弦乐四重奏》和《大提琴协奏曲》等重要作品。在美国期间，他鼓励美国作曲家发展民族音乐风格，对美国音乐教育产生了深远影响。1895年，他因思乡心切返回捷克，但这段美国经历极大地丰富了他的音乐创作。
points.descriptionEn: Dvořák was invited to serve as director of the National Conservatory of Music in America, spending three years in the United States. During this period, he composed his famous 'New World Symphony', incorporating elements of African American spirituals and Native American music. He also created important works like the 'American String Quartet' and 'Cello Concerto'. In America, he encouraged American composers to develop a national musical style, leaving a profound impact on American music education. In 1895, he returned to Czechoslovakia due to homesickness, but this American experience greatly enriched his musical compositions.

points.title: 晚年辉煌
points.description: 返回布拉格后，德沃夏克继续创作和教学。1896年，他创作了歌剧《水仙女》，成为捷克民族歌剧的代表作。1901年，他被任命为布拉格音乐学院院长，成为捷克音乐界的领袖人物。晚年，他创作了多部交响乐、室内乐和歌剧作品，包括《圣经歌曲》和《英雄之歌》。1904年，德沃夏克在布拉格去世，享年62岁。他的音乐作品融合了民族特色和古典传统，对世界音乐产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Prague, Dvořák continued to compose and teach. In 1896, he composed the opera 'Rusalka', which became a masterpiece of Czech national opera. In 1901, he was appointed director of the Prague Conservatory, becoming a leading figure in Czech music. In his later years, he composed numerous symphonies, chamber works, and operas, including 'Biblical Songs' and 'The Hero's Song'. Dvořák died in Prague in 1904 at the age of 62. His musical works, which blend national characteristics with classical tradition, have had a profound impact on world music.

supporter.zh: 德沃夏克被视为民族乐派的杰出代表，他将波西米亚民间音乐元素融入古典音乐形式，创造了独特的音乐语言。他的作品充满热情和生命力，尤其是《新世界交响曲》和《斯拉夫舞曲》等作品，展现了民族自豪感和文化自信。作为教育家，他培养了众多优秀音乐人才，对美国和捷克音乐教育贡献卓著。德沃夏克的音乐跨越了民族界限，成为世界文化遗产的重要组成部分。
supporter.en: Dvořák is regarded as an outstanding representative of the national school of music, integrating Bohemian folk elements into classical forms to create a unique musical language. His works are filled with passion and vitality, especially pieces like the 'New World Symphony' and 'Slavonic Dances', which demonstrate national pride and cultural confidence. As an educator, he trained numerous talented musicians, making significant contributions to music education in America and the Czech Republic. Dvořák's music transcends national boundaries, becoming an important part of world cultural heritage.

critic.zh: 批评者认为德沃夏克的作品有时过于依赖民族元素，缺乏创新性和深度。他的某些作品被认为结构松散，形式不够严谨。此外，他在美国期间创作的《新世界交响曲》被批评为对非裔美国人音乐元素的表面化运用，缺乏真正的理解和尊重。还有人指出，德沃夏克在国际上的成功部分得益于勃拉姆斯的推荐，而非完全依靠自身才华，这削弱了他作为独立艺术家的地位。
critic.en: Critics argue that Dvořák's works sometimes rely too heavily on national elements, lacking innovation and depth. Some of his compositions are considered structurally loose and not rigorously formed. Additionally, his 'New World Symphony' composed in America has been criticized for superficial use of African American musical elements without genuine understanding and respect. Some also suggest that his international success was partly due to Brahms' recommendations rather than solely his own talent, which diminishes his status as an independent artist.

objective.zh: 从历史和流行文化视角看，德沃夏克被定义为连接欧洲古典传统与民族音乐的重要桥梁。他的作品既保持了古典音乐的结构严谨性，又融入了丰富的民族特色，影响了后世众多作曲家。在流行文化中，《新世界交响曲》第二乐章成为广泛传播的经典旋律，被用于电影、广告等多种场合。德沃夏克的音乐教育理念，特别是对民族音乐价值的肯定，对20世纪世界音乐教育产生了深远影响，使他成为音乐史上不可或缺的重要人物。
objective.en: From a historical and popular culture perspective, Dvořák is defined as an important bridge connecting European classical tradition with national music. His works maintained the structural rigor of classical music while incorporating rich national characteristics, influencing many later composers. In popular culture, the second movement of the 'New World Symphony' has become a widely recognized classic melody, used in films, advertisements, and other contexts. Dvořák's music education philosophy, particularly his affirmation of the value of national music, has had a profound impact on 20th-century global music education, making him an indispensable figure in music history.

self.zh: 我的音乐是捷克人民的灵魂，是波西米亚森林和田野的声音。
self.en: My music is the soul of the Czech people, the sound of the Bohemian forests and fields.

others.zh: 德沃夏克是一位真正的音乐天才，他的作品充满了原创性和力量，是当代最伟大的作曲家之一。
others.en: Dvořák is a true musical genius whose works are filled with originality and power, one of the greatest composers of our time.
